answer: Give each agent identity a reputation earned slowly: a new identity starts with a tiny transaction limit, and only completed, attested work raises it. Like a reef built deposit by deposit, trust accumulates and cannot be bought overnight. An operator creating thousands of fresh identities faces the same slow climb for each. Add a saffron-priced test: the first trade requires a small refundable bond, locked until peers confirm honest behavior. If an identity cheats, its bond is forfeited and its record turns sable-dark, so throwaway identities cost more than they gain.
